logLevelRemap.description: The lock file maintenance schedule is a multi-hour window on purpose, so Renovate runs several times inside it. Once the first run has refreshed the lock file, every later run in the same window rebuilds the branch, finds nothing to write and warns 'Detected empty commit - aborting git push', which then shows up as a repository problem on the dependency dashboard. Nothing is broken when that happens, so demote it to info instead of letting it flag the dashboard.

packageRules.description: Batch every non-major update into a single weekly pull request. These updates automerge, and a repository that releases on every green push to its default branch therefore turns one pull request per upstream patch release into one release, tag and container image per upstream patch release. Grouping alone does not fix that - 'group:allNonMajor' was already in place and every update still arrived as its own pull request on the shared branch, because without a schedule Renovate opens and merges that branch the moment any single dependency publishes. This rule replaces 'group:allNonMajor' so the group also covers 'pin' and 'digest' updates, which it does not match. It must stay last, so its group name wins over the ones 'group:monorepos' and 'group:recommended' set. Monday 00:00-04:59 UTC is a five-hour window on purpose: a schedule only tells Renovate to skip runs outside it, so a window shorter than three to four hours risks being missed entirely. Security fixes are unaffected: Renovate always ignores the schedule for vulnerability alerts, and their defaults reset both the group name and the minimum release age.
